title: Flash Eurobarometer 578
text:
European Commission: Growing use of AI in European companies

WhoEuropean Commission, DG EMPL
When2026
WhereEU-27
SampleFirms12,826 SMEs and mid-caps (1 to 749 employees)
QuestionDoes the company use AI or algorithmic management, and what drives or
holds back adoption?
AdoptionFirms: 42%

Main aim. To identify what drives and what hinders the adoption of AI and
algorithmic management in smaller companies, with a focus on workplace
issues.

title: ECFIN consumer survey
text:
DG ECFIN: AI at work in Europe (European Business Cycle Indicators, Q1
2026)

WhoEuropean Commission, DG ECFIN
When2026
Where18 EU Member States
SampleIndividuals21,207 consumers
Question“Are you using AI technologies for your work or for personal tasks?”
AdoptionIndividuals: 54% · Workers: 34.5% (employed, all ages)

Main aim. To measure consumer confidence each month. A one-off module in early
2026 asked how people use AI and how they think it affects their
productivity, quality of work and job security.

title: Digital Decade EB
text:
Special Eurobarometer 572: The Digital Decade 2026

WhoEuropean Commission, DG CNECT
When2026
WhereEU-27
SampleIndividuals26,494 people aged 15+
Question“How often do you use generative AI tools? In your personal life / In
your work, or your studies”
AdoptionIndividuals: 61%

Main aim. To track citizens’ views on the digital transformation and the EU’s
Digital Decade priorities. The 2026 edition asked for the first time how
often people use generative AI tools.

title: EU-OSHA OSH Pulse
text:
EU-OSHA: OSH Pulse 2025

WhoEU-OSHA
When2025
WhereEU-27 (plus Iceland, Norway, Switzerland)
SampleWorkers25,688 people in employment aged 16+ in the EU
Question“Do you use any of the following digital technologies for your main job?
[…] Software or tools powered by artificial intelligence”
AdoptionWorkers: 18% (employed, aged 16+)

Main aim. To take a quick reading of workers’ safety and health, this time with a
focus on climate change and digitalisation. AI appears among the digital
technologies workers use in their main job.

title: Eurostat individuals
text:
Eurostat: 64% of 16-24-year-olds used AI in 2025

WhoEurostat
When2025
WhereEU-27
SampleIndividualsPeople aged 16 to 74
QuestionDid you use generative AI tools in the last three months, and for what
purpose (private, work, formal education)?
AdoptionIndividuals: 32.7%

Main aim. To produce official, comparable statistics on how people use the
internet and digital technologies. Questions on generative AI were asked
for the first time in 2025.

title: EIB Investment Survey
text:
EIB Investment Survey 2025: European Union overview

WhoEuropean Investment Bank
When2025
WhereEU-27 (plus a US sample)
SampleFirms12,033 firms
QuestionTwo questions combined: whether the firm has implemented “Big data
analytics and artificial intelligence”, and “I would like to ask about
your company’s systematic use of generative AI tools to improve
processes. […] Does your company invest in these kinds of tools in any
of the following areas?”
AdoptionFirms: 37% (EIB measure of firms using generative AI, built from a big data and AI
question and a generative AI investment question; weighted by value
added. Not comparable with the 2026 wave)

Main aim. To track firms’ investment activity, financing needs and obstacles to
investment across the EU. Generative AI was added as part of the section
on digital technologies.

The EIB labels this chart “Firms using generative AI”, and the note under it lists two questions: whether the firm uses big data analytics and artificial intelligence, and whether it invests in generative AI tools (overview, p. 27). The EIB does not say how the two answers are combined. The sector figures suggest a firm must answer yes to both: 39% of manufacturing firms and 36% of service firms are counted here, while 48% and 41% use big data and AI (p. 25), and a measure counting a yes to either question could not be lower than that. Shares are weighted by value added (“About this publication”), whereas Eurostat’s 20% for 2025 counts each firm equally; Bick et al. find that reweighting Eurostat’s data by value added gives levels close to the EIBIS ones (St. Louis Fed Working Paper 2026-003B, Section 3.2 and Appendix C.1; the NBER version, w34995, does not include this comparison).

title: Bick et al.
text:
Bick, Blandin, Deming, Fuchs-Schündeln and Jessen: Mind the Gap: AI
Adoption in Europe and the U.S.

WhoBick, Blandin, Deming, Fuchs-Schündeln and Jessen (academic survey)
When2025
WhereGermany, France, Italy, Netherlands, Sweden (plus UK and US)
SampleWorkersAbout 5,000 per country, employed, aged 18 to 67 (18 to 63 in France)
Question“Do you use Generative AI for your job?”
AdoptionWorkers: 30% (employed, aged 18-67; simple mean of the five EU countries)

Main aim. To measure generative AI use at work in a way that is comparable between
the United States and Europe, using the same questionnaire in every
country, and to estimate the time workers save.

title: Eurostat enterprises
text:
Eurostat: Usage of AI technologies increasing in EU enterprises

WhoEurostat
When2024
WhereEU-27
SampleFirmsEnterprises with 10+ employees
QuestionDoes the enterprise use any of a list of AI technologies (text mining,
speech recognition, language generation, image recognition, machine
learning, process automation, autonomous machines)?
AdoptionFirms: 13.5%

Main aim. To produce official, comparable statistics on how businesses use digital
technologies, for monitoring the EU’s Digital Decade targets. AI is one
module among several.

title: Eurobarometer 554
text:
Special Eurobarometer 554: Artificial Intelligence and the future of
work

WhoEuropean Commission, DG EMPL
When2024
WhereEU-27
SampleIndividuals26,415 people aged 15+
Question“How positively or negatively do you perceive the use of robots and
Artificial Intelligence in the workplace?”
AdoptionNo adoption question

Main aim. To gauge public attitudes towards AI and digital technology in the
workplace, including support for rules on how employers use them. It
measures opinions rather than use.

title: Cedefop AI skills
text:
Cedefop: first insights from the AI skills survey

WhoCedefop
When2024
Where11 EU countries
SampleWorkers5,342 employees aged 16 to 64
Question“To the best of your knowledge, do you or your colleagues use any AI
tools or systems at your workplace?”
AdoptionWorkplace: 28% say they or colleagues use AI at work; no personal-use
rate is published

Main aim. To measure how AI is changing skill needs at work: who works with AI,
which tasks it changes, and whether workers have the skills and training
to keep up. It follows up Cedefop’s second European skills and jobs
survey.

title: Country evidence
text: National surveys with their own AI questions, from central banks, statistical offices and research institutes. They cover one country each, so they are not plotted on the overview.

title: Country evidence
text:
Germany
ifo Business Survey · ifo Institute · May 2026 · Firms, about 9,000. Asks whether AI is in use, planned, under discussion, or not an issue.

Bundesbank Online Panel Firms · Deutsche Bundesbank, Monthly Report March 2026, box “Generative AI in German enterprises: adoption, costs and expected economic impact” (pp. 109-110) · April to June 2025 · Firms, more than 7,000. “Has your enterprise already used generative artificial intelligence (AI) or is it planning to use it in future?”, asked for 2024, 2025 and 2026.

IAB Establishment Panel · Institute for Employment Research · July to November 2025 · Firms, about 15,000 establishments of all sizes. Asks whether the establishment uses generative AI, and since when.

DiWaBe 2.0 · BAuA, ZEW, IAB and BIBB · July to December 2024 · Workers, 9,835 employees aged 16 to 65. “How often do you work with AI-supported computer programs?”

title: Country evidence
text:
France
Monthly business survey, AI module · Banque de France · 25 February to 3 April 2026 · Firms, about 7,000; results for those with 20+ employees. Asks what use the firm makes of generative and non-generative AI: intensive, limited, experimental, planned, or none.

title: Country evidence
text:
Italy
Survey of Industrial and Service Firms · Banca d’Italia · 17 February to 12 May 2026 · Firms, about 4,000 with 20+ employees. Asks what use the firm makes of predictive and generative AI: extensive, limited, experimental, planned, or none.

title: Country evidence
text:
Spain
Business Activity Survey (EBAE) · Banco de España · 11 to 25 November 2024 · Firms, about 6,300 of all sizes. Asks how much the firm uses predictive and generative AI: none, planned, sporadic or pilot, moderate, or high.

title: Country evidence
text:
Austria
AI use and attitudes · Statistics Austria · April to July 2025 · Individuals, 5,550 people aged 16 to 74. Asks whether people have used AI tools to generate text, images or other content, and how often in the last three months.

title: Country evidence
text:
Netherlands
Belevingen 2025, AI module · Statistics Netherlands (CBS) · 23 January to 30 June 2025 · Individuals, 3,834 adults aged 18+; the work question goes to those in paid work. “Gebruikt u op dit moment kunstmatige intelligentie voor uw werk?” (Do you currently use artificial intelligence for your work?)

Employers’ Survey on Work (WEA) 2024 · TNO · 15 January to 29 May 2024 · Firms, 3,460 establishments with 5+ employees. Asks which technologies the establishment uses, including “algorithms, artificial intelligence (AI) or big data techniques to improve processes, products or services”.

title: Country evidence
text:
Denmark
AI chatbot adoption surveys · Humlum and Vestergaard, fielded by Statistics Denmark · November to December 2024 (first wave late 2023) · Workers, 25,241 in 11 AI-exposed occupations covering about a fifth of Danish employment. “Har du benyttet følgende AI chatbots?” (Have you used the following AI chatbots?), with answers for work and for leisure.

title: Country evidence
text:
Finland
Generative AI module, EVA values and attitudes survey · ETLA · 8 to 21 October 2024 · Individuals, 2,018 people aged 18 to 79. Asks how often people used an AI web application in the last 12 months, and whether they have used AI for a task in their job.

Working Life Barometer 2025 · Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment, data collected by Statistics Finland · autumn 2025 · Workers, wage earners aged 18 to 64. Asks whether AI technology is used at the respondent’s workplace, and with what effects.

title: Country evidence
text:
Poland
NBP Quick Monitoring Survey · Narodowy Bank Polski · quarterly; AI questions in the reports for Q4 2024 and Q2 2026 · Firms, non-financial enterprises of all sizes. Asks whether the firm uses AI tools or plans to. Figures are taken from press reports of the survey, not from the NBP publication itself.

title: Company surveys
text: Surveys run or commissioned by private companies. Most use online panels and loose definitions of “using AI”, and publish little on method, so they are not plotted on the overview.

title: Company surveys
text:
AWS / Strand Partners
Unlocking Europe’s AI Potential 2026 · Amazon Web Services, fieldwork by Strand Partners · published March 2026, fieldwork dates not stated · Firms, 17,000 business leaders in 17 European countries (14 in the EU). Asks whether the business has adopted AI; exact wording not published.

title: Company surveys
text:
SD Worx
HR and Payroll Pulse 2026 · SD Worx, fieldwork by iVOX · 27 January to 20 February 2026 · Workers and firms, 16,500 employees and 5,936 HR decision-makers in 16 European countries (13 in the EU). Asks whether and how often employees use AI at work; exact wording not published.

title: Company surveys
text:
EY
European AI Barometer 2025 · EY · March 2025 · Workers, 4,942 managers and employees in 9 Western European countries (8 in the EU). “Have you ever been involved with Artificial Intelligence (for example ChatGPT, Perplexity, Midjourney) or have you actively used it?”

title: Company surveys
text:
Deloitte
Trust in generative AI: a European perspective · Deloitte · 28 June to 12 August 2024 · Individuals, 30,252 people aged 16 to 75 in 11 European countries (9 in the EU). “Have you ever used any generative AI tools, or not?”

title: GenAI Surveys in Europe
text:
A list of surveys on artificial intelligence run in Europe, kept by DG EMPL and DG ECFIN of the European Commission. Surveys are grouped by year in the menu on the left; each page gives who ran the survey, when, where, whether workers or firms were asked, and the main result.

title: EU-OSHA ESENER
text:
EU-OSHA: ESENER 2024 first findings

WhoEU-OSHA
When2024
WhereEU-27 (plus Iceland, Norway, Switzerland)
SampleFirms41,458 establishments with 5+ employees
Question“Does your establishment use any of the following digital technologies
for work? […] Machines, systems or computers that use Artificial
Intelligence to perform work tasks”
AdoptionFirms: 7% (establishments with 5+ employees)

Main aim. To find out how European workplaces manage safety and health risks. AI
is covered as one of several digital technologies that may create new
risks for workers.

title: Eurofound EWCS
text:
Eurofound: EWCS 2024 first findings

WhoEurofound
When2024
Where35 European countries
SampleWorkers36,644 people
Question“At work, do you use artificial intelligence that simplifies complex
mental tasks or makes recommendations (e.g. ChatGPT, LLAMA, DALL-E,
Midjourney, Jasper)?”
AdoptionWorkers: 12% (workers, all ages)

Main aim. To monitor working conditions and job quality across Europe. The AI
question is one item in a long questionnaire on tasks, autonomy, work
intensity and health.
12% of EU workers use generative AI tools at work. Among EU countries the share runs from 5% or less in Greece, Italy, Portugal and Romania to at least one in five in Luxembourg, Sweden, Belgium and Denmark (Eurofound overview report, pp. 27-28). Across all 35 countries surveyed, the range is from under 3% (Bosnia-Herzegovina) to about 25% (Luxembourg).

title: JRC AIM-WORK
text:
JRC: Digital monitoring, algorithmic management and the platformisation
of work in Europe

WhoEuropean Commission, JRC and DG EMPL
When2024-25
WhereEU-27
SampleWorkers70,316 people aged 16 to 65
Question“In the last 12 months, did you use an AI-powered tool when performing
your main paid job?”
AdoptionWorkers: 30% (workers aged 16-65)

Main aim. To measure how common AI tools, digital monitoring and algorithmic
management are in European workplaces, and how they relate to working
conditions.

title: ECB SAFE
text:
ECB Occasional Paper 395: Adoption and investment in AI across the euro
area

WhoEuropean Central Bank
When2025
Where12 euro area countries (AT, BE, DE, EL, ES, FI, FR, IE, IT, NL, PT, SK)
SampleFirms5,067 firms in the December 2025 round; results weighted by employment
Question“How would you assess the use of AI technologies in your firm?”
AdoptionFirms: 38% (moderate or significant use; 71% including very infrequent or pilot use)

Main aim. To monitor the financing conditions of euro area firms for monetary
policy. The AI questions were a one-off addition asking how intensively
firms use AI and what holds them back.

title: Eurostat enterprises
text:
Eurostat: Use of artificial intelligence in enterprises

WhoEurostat
When2025
WhereEU-27
SampleFirms157,000 enterprises with 10+ employees
QuestionDoes the enterprise use any of eight AI technologies (text mining,
speech recognition, language generation, image generation, image
recognition, machine learning, process automation, autonomous machines)?
AdoptionFirms: 20%

Main aim. To produce official, comparable statistics on how businesses use digital
technologies, for monitoring the EU’s Digital Decade targets. AI is one
module among several.

title: Flash Eurobarometer 559
text:
Flash Eurobarometer 559: Startups, scaleups and entrepreneurship

WhoEuropean Commission, DG GROW
When2025
WhereEU-27 (plus 11 non-EU countries)
SampleFirms12,653 SMEs with 1 to 249 employees in the EU
Question“Which of the following advanced technologies, if any, has your
enterprise adopted to date? […] Artificial intelligence, e.g. machine
learning, Large Language Models”
AdoptionFirms: 14%

Main aim. To understand the conditions for starting and scaling up a business in
the EU. AI adoption is one item in a list of advanced technologies firms
may have taken up.

title: Bick et al.
text:
Bick, Blandin, Deming, Fuchs-Schündeln and Jessen: Mind the Gap: AI
Adoption in Europe and the U.S.

WhoBick, Blandin, Deming, Fuchs-Schündeln and Jessen (academic survey)
When2026
WhereGermany, France, Italy, Netherlands, Sweden (plus UK and US)
SampleWorkersAbout 3,000 per country, employed, aged 18 to 67 (18 to 63 in France)
Question“Do you use Generative AI for your job?”
AdoptionWorkers: 31.3% (employed, aged 18-67; simple mean of the five EU countries)

Main aim. To measure generative AI use at work in a way that is comparable between
the United States and Europe, using the same questionnaire in every
country, and to see how adoption changed since the 2025 wave.

title: ECB CES
text:
ECB Blog: AI adoption and the productivity promise: what workers report

WhoEuropean Central Bank
When2024, 2025 and 2026
Where11 euro area countries
SampleWorkersConsumer Expectations Survey, about 20,000 people per month
Question“Do you personally use artificial intelligence (AI) in your work
(including tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, etc.)?”
AdoptionWorkers: 52% (employed, all ages)

Main aim. To monitor euro area households’ expectations and economic behaviour for
monetary policy. The AI questions ask workers whether they use AI in
their job and how much time it saves them.

title: EIB Investment Survey
text:
EIB Group Investment Survey 2026: European Union overview

WhoEuropean Investment Bank
When2026
WhereEU-27 (plus a US sample)
SampleFirms12,083 firms
Question“I would like to ask about your company’s systematic use of generative
AI tools to improve processes. […] Does your company use these kinds of
tools in any of the following areas?”
AdoptionFirms: 67% (use of generative AI tools only. The 2025 figure combined a big data and
AI question with a question on investing in generative AI tools, so the
two waves are not comparable)

Main aim. To track firms’ investment activity, financing needs and obstacles to
investment across the EU. The generative AI questions ask in which
business areas firms use these tools.
